title: Salesforce Service Cloud alternatives for B2B support | Pylon
summary: Compare 7 Service Cloud alternatives on entry prices, AI billing, and B2B fit. Decide whether to keep Salesforce CRM or stay on Service Cloud.
body_markdown:
You can keep Salesforce as your CRM and replace Service Cloud as your support platform. Evaluate that split when sales needs Salesforce but support needs different customer channels, investigation workflows, or day-to-day controls.


Stay on Service Cloud when its data model, service operations, and administration are a good fit. Moving software is not an improvement if it recreates the same dependencies elsewhere.


The 7 alternatives below cover different needs: Pylon for account-aware B2B support, Zendesk for a configurable support suite, Freshdesk for a lower paid entry point, Intercom for in-app support, HubSpot Service Hub for CRM consolidation, Plain for technical B2B support, and Help Scout for inbox-led teams.


Disclosure: this post is published by Pylon. We stick to what each vendor says on its own public pages, checked Nov 6, 2026.


## First, compare the right Salesforce baseline


Salesforce's[current Service Cloud pricing page](https://www.salesforce.com/service/pricing/) lists Starter Suite, Pro Suite, Core, Advanced, and Max. The comparison table shows Starter Suite at $25 per user/month, Pro Suite at $100, Core at $195, Advanced at $395, and Max at $550. The page marks Core, Advanced, and Max as annual-contract editions; Starter Suite can be billed monthly or annually.


Those are not identical service bundles. A low-entry CRM suite is not a substitute for pricing the full support configuration your team runs. Salesforce's page also lists AI, digital channels, contact-center products, and other capabilities whose packaging depends on edition.


Use your actual renewal proposal as the baseline. Include the required edition, AI consumption, channel products, implementation, administration, and integrations. Don't compare an enterprise deployment with a competitor's bare entry seat and call the difference savings.

## 1. Pylon: keep Salesforce CRM, change how support works


Pylon is the agentic support platform purpose-built for B2B. It is the full help desk, not an AI layer attached to Service Cloud.


Its[Salesforce integration docs](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/integrations/crm/salesforce) describe account matching, field sync in either direction, contact sync, account details beside issues, and daily conversation-summary activity sync. That gives you a concrete way to keep commercial data in Salesforce while moving support work to Pylon.


Agents do more than draft replies. Assist Agent investigates and acts for teammates, Support Agent works on customer questions, Slack Agent answers and acts from Slack, and Automations start repeatable work from events or schedules. Set to start on new issues, agents investigate issues before your team opens them. Skills define reusable instructions.[Nexus](https://www.usepylon.com/nexus) describes the context, runtime permissions, approvals, and traces behind those workflows.


Professional is $89 per seat/month and Advanced is $139 on annual contracts. Enterprise is custom. Agentic features use credits, with committed packages starting at 5,000 credits/year. Slack is on every plan; Teams and Google Chat require Advanced or Enterprise. Account Intelligence is a separate add-on.


**Tradeoff:** you are replacing the help desk, so plan the queue, workflows, historical data, reporting, and integrations. If you want only an agent on top of Service Cloud, Pylon is not that product.


## 2. Zendesk: a support suite with substantial configuration


Zendesk's entry Support Team plan covers email and support essentials. Suite Team adds messaging, live chat, knowledge base, and telephony. Higher tiers add further routing, governance, and other capabilities.


AI agents use automated-resolution billing, and Copilot has an optional per-seat model. Your comparison should include the Suite configuration and add-ons needed, not only the $19 entry price.


**Choose it when:** you want a dedicated support suite with the configuration options listed on its pricing page. Test the exact B2B customer channel and account workflow rather than assuming every integration behaves the same way.


## 3. Freshdesk: a lower paid entry point


Freshdesk Growth includes an email-focused shared inbox, portal, and knowledge base at $19 per agent/month billed annually. Pro adds intelligent routing, multiple SLA policies, and custom reporting. Enterprise adds further routing and governance capabilities.


Freddy AI Agent uses sessions. The initial 500-session allowance is once per account. Copilot is an optional per-seat add-on on Pro and Enterprise.


**Choose it when:** your support operation fits the channel and workflow scope of the plan you price. Replacing a broader deployment may require a different Freshworks configuration than Growth.


## 4. Intercom: in-app support with Fin


Essential includes Messenger, shared inbox, a public help center, and prebuilt reports. Advanced adds workflows; Expert lists SLAs and identity management. Fin can take actions on external systems and hand work to a human inbox, according to Intercom's pricing page.


Fin is billed per outcome. Its outcome definition can include completion of a Procedure with a handoff, so align the billing definition with your own resolution reporting.


**Choose it when:** product and in-app conversations are central to support. If the plan is to replace Service Cloud, separate that from buying Fin for an existing help desk, which the vendor also offers. Those are different deployment choices.


## 5. HubSpot Service Hub: consider the CRM decision separately


HubSpot offers a free edition and paid entry seats from $20 per seat/month billed monthly. Its page lists help desk workspace, Customer Agent, knowledge base, and customer success workspace at Professional. Customer Agent uses credits for delivered resolutions, per its[documentation](https://knowledge.hubspot.com/customer-agent/understand-the-customer-agent) .


Service Hub is part of HubSpot's customer platform. It also lists a supported Salesforce integration for Professional and Enterprise customers, so using it doesn't automatically require replacing Salesforce CRM.


**Choose it when:** shared customer data with HubSpot is valuable. Decide explicitly whether the project changes service software, CRM, or both, then assign an owner to every synchronized field.


## 6. Plain: technical B2B support in shared channels


Plain Foundation includes Slack, email, in-app channels, and Linear and Jira integrations at $45 per user/month billed annually. Horizon is $99 and adds Teams, SLAs, business hours, and CRM integrations.


Its[Slack docs](https://www.plain.com/docs/product/channels/slack) describe messages becoming threads in Plain and replies returning to Slack. Customer Agent handles assigned customer threads; Sidekick works for teammates. AI uses workspace credits.


**Choose it when:** the technical support workflow fits. Horizon is the meaningful comparison when SLAs or CRM sync are requirements. Foundation's lower entry price does not include every operational feature.


## 7. Help Scout: an inbox-led alternative


Help Scout offers a free edition, Standard at a displayed $25 per user/month, and Plus at $45. Plus and Pro group conversations by company; Plus lists Salesforce, Jira, and HubSpot integrations.


Help Scout is not limited to email. Paid channels include live chat, SMS, WhatsApp, Instagram, and Messenger. It has tiered SLAs and Envoy, billed per resolution. Its[native Slack integration](https://docs.helpscout.com/article/271-connect-slack-with-help-scout-get-notifications-in-slack) is notifications-only, not a customer support channel.


**Choose it when:** your team's channels and account needs fit that model. It is not an equivalent replacement for every complex Service Cloud operation, and it doesn't need to be.


## Keep Salesforce CRM, or stay all-in?


### Keep CRM and replace Service Cloud when the boundary is clear


This split is worth testing when sales wants Salesforce accounts and opportunities but support needs a different queue, channel experience, or investigation process.


Define the boundary before migration:


- Which platform owns accounts, contacts, commercial fields, and support commitments?
- Which fields sync, in which direction, and how are conflicts resolved?
- Where do people find the authoritative support history?
- Which automations need a service event, a CRM update, or a human approval?
- Who owns integration failures and reporting reconciliation?


Pylon's documented Salesforce sync makes this a concrete operating option. It does not imply every custom object, Flow, entitlement, report, or historical record transfers automatically.


### Stay all-in when the existing platform earns its place


Service Cloud may remain the better fit if your operation depends on its service data model, entitlements, contact-center configuration, or shared Salesforce processes, and your team has the administration capacity to maintain them.


Salesforce's current pricing page lists case management, service contracts and entitlements, routing, Slack collaboration, AI, and contact-center options. It is not accurate to describe it as "unable to use AI" or "unable to take actions." The buying decision is whether your configured system serves your team better than the alternative after total cost and change risk are included.


Run a real workflow through both paths. Compare time to change the process, correctness of the investigation, human handoff, and the bill at 1× and 2× volume. Include the work of maintaining either platform.


## Make the migration decision with a sample, not a promise


Inventory active cases, account mappings, users, attachments, knowledge base structure, reporting, and destination workflows. Decide how open conversations remain replyable. Validate a sample before setting cutover dates.


Avoid vendor-specific migration timing promises that aren't documented for your scope. Your renewal proposal and validated migration plan matter more than a generic implementation claim.


If keeping Salesforce CRM while changing support is the right boundary,[book a demo](https://www.usepylon.com/schedule-demo) . Bring an account-specific issue and the Salesforce fields your team needs to resolve it.


## FAQ


### Can we replace Service Cloud without replacing Salesforce CRM?


Yes. For example, Pylon documents a Salesforce integration for account matching, field sync, contacts, activity summaries, and account details beside issues. Define data ownership and test the required workflows before cutover.


### What is the best Salesforce Service Cloud alternative for B2B support?


Our editorial choice for account-aware support in Slack, Teams, email, and chat is Pylon. Zendesk, Freshdesk, Intercom, HubSpot Service Hub, Plain, and Help Scout fit different channel, CRM, and operating requirements.


### Is Service Cloud always more expensive?


No. A fair comparison includes the current Salesforce contract and an alternative configured for equivalent requirements, including AI, channels, implementation, integration, and operating work.


### Is Pylon an AI add-on for Service Cloud?


No. Pylon is the full help desk. Salesforce can remain connected as the CRM while support runs in Pylon.
